title: Wildcard Match
statement:
A **pattern** can contain lowercase letters and two wildcards:

- `?` matches **any single letter**,
- `*` matches **any sequence of letters**, including an empty sequence.

The pattern must match the **whole** `text`, not just a part of it. Return `true` if `pattern` matches `text`, otherwise `false`. Either string may be empty.
constraints: text contains only lowercase letters; pattern contains lowercase letters, ? and *

examples.explanation: The pattern covers only one letter.
The first * matches the empty string, a matches a, the second * matches dce, and b matches b.

hints.nudge: Look at the last character of the pattern. What are the cases: letter, ?, or *?
hints.pattern: Dynamic programming on prefixes: match(i, j) = does the first i letters of text match the first j pattern characters?
hints.pseudocode:
match(0, 0) = true; match(0, j) = match(0, j-1) if pattern[j-1] == '*' else false
match(i, j):
  if pattern[j-1] == '*': match(i, j-1) or match(i-1, j)      // * matches nothing, or one more letter
  else: match(i-1, j-1) and (pattern[j-1] == '?' or pattern[j-1] == text[i-1])
hints.walkthrough: A `*` makes plain recursion branch a lot, so remember the results for each pair (i, j): match(i, j) says whether the first i text letters match the first j pattern characters. For an ordinary letter or `?`, the last characters must fit and the earlier parts must match: match(i-1, j-1). For `*`, either it matches nothing (match(i, j-1)) or it swallows one more text letter (match(i-1, j)). The base cases: two empty prefixes match, and an empty text matches only a run of `*`. A table of (n + 1) * (m + 1) booleans gives O(n * m).
